desc: Ideation: Derive that building i is visible iff h > M_i = max_{j<i} T_{j,i}, where T_{j,i} is the y-intercept of the line through (X_j, H_j) and (X_i, H_i). The answer is max(0, max_i M_i) if >0 else -1.
Implement the O(N) algorithm using a deque for the upper convex hull and a moving pointer to compute M_i for each building, tracking the global maximum.
After processing all buildings, if global_max <= 0, print -1; else print global_max with high precision (e.g., 18 decimal places).

Refine pointer adjustment: When popping points from the hull, if the popped point was at or after `ptr`, adjust `ptr` accordingly (e.g., decrement if needed) to ensure it points to a valid hull element.
Test the algorithm on all provided sample inputs (Samples 1-4) and confirm outputs match expected values.
Verify with random tests against a brute-force O(N^2) implementation for small N to ensure correctness.
